outputs.exact_statement:
For every finite $n\ge0$, every $u:\Omega_n\to[-1,1]$, and $-1\le\rho\le1$, $$I(T_\rho u)
 \le\psi\!\left(|\rho|\,\psi^{-1}(I(u))\right).
 \label{main:interpolation}$$ The inverse is the nonnegative increasing branch on $[0,L]$. For $n\ge1$, every soft coordinate $u(x)=a x_i$, $|a|\le1$, attains equality.

For every finite $n\ge0$, $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and $f:\Omega_n\to\{-1,1\}$, put $m=\mathbb Ef$ and $r_m=\psi^{-1}(H(m))$. Then $$I(f(X);Y)\le\psi(|\rho|r_m)\le\psi(|\rho|).
 \label{main:bound}$$ For $n\ge1$, signed coordinate functions attain the bound at $m=0$. If $0<|m|<1$ and $0<|\rho|\le1$, the refined upper curve is strictly below the universal curve $\psi(|\rho|)$.

For every finite $n\ge0$ and every $g:\{-1,1\}^n\to(-1,1)$, with $m=\mathbb Eg$, $$D(g)\ge\widehat{\mathcal B}_m(I(g))
       =\max\{\mathcal B_m(I(g)),F(I(g))\}
       \ge F(I(g)).
 \label{upgrade:production-bound}$$
The function $I\mapsto e^{-2I}F''(I)$ is strictly increasing on $[0,L)$. For $I>0$ it satisfies $$\frac{F'''(I)}{F''(I)}>2.$$

For every $p\ge0$, the minimum of $$\mathbb E\{c(A,B)+p[H(A)+H(B)]\}, \qquad \mathbb EA=a,\quad \mathbb EB=b,$$ has a unique optimizer. It is one ordered interior pair $(x,y)$ and possible equal corners, as in [canonical:law]. Its core is given by the unique minimizer of $F_p$ subject to [canonical:floors], using [canonical:coordinates]; its masses are [canonical:masses]. At $p=0$, the optimizer is the deterministic pair $(a,b)$.

Let $g(X)=m+\delta X$, where $X$ is a uniform sign and $|m|+|\delta|<1$. Write $\alpha=1-m^2$ and $$J=\frac{\psi(m+\delta)+\psi(m-\delta)}2-\psi(m),
 \qquad D=\frac\delta2\{V(m+\delta)-V(m-\delta)\}.$$ Then $J<\alpha L$ and $$D\ge\alpha F(J/\alpha).
 \label{capacity:refined}$$

For $-1<m<1$ and $0\le\delta<1-|m|$, put $$A=1-m,\qquad
 \kappa=\frac12\log\frac1{1-\delta^2/(1+m)^2}.$$ Then $$A^2\log\frac\alpha\beta\le3\kappa.
 \label{reserve:log-geometry}$$

For every physical state $(m,\delta,e)$ and $0<\tau\le1$, $$W(1-\tau+\tau m,\tau\delta,\tau e)
 \le\tau W(m,\delta,e).
 \label{reserve:plus-corner}$$ The same inequality holds with parent mean $-1+\tau+\tau m$, corresponding to the negative common output. There is no sign restriction on the original mean.

Let $(A,B)$ have any joint law on $[-1,1]^2$ with $e_a=\mathbb EH(A)>0$ and $e_b=\mathbb EH(B)>0$. Put $$a=\mathbb EA,\quad b=\mathbb EB,\quad m=\frac{a+b}{2},
 \quad e=\frac{e_a+e_b}{2},$$ and $I=H(m)-e$, $I_a=H(a)-e_a$, $I_b=H(b)-e_b$. Then $$\mathbb Ec(A,B)\ge
 \mathcal B_m(I)-\frac{\mathcal B_a(I_a)+\mathcal B_b(I_b)}2.
 \label{reserve:local-bound}$$
For the core and mass in [thinning:path], $$\label{thinning:value} F(\nu+J)-F(\nu)\le\lambda F(J_c).$$

Let $0\le x<1$, and put $$p=1+x,\qquad \sigma=1-x,\qquad
 \gamma=\frac{\sigma}{p},\qquad
 \beta=\frac{\log(1+x)}L.$$ Suppose $$0\le z<\gamma,\qquad \sigma-pz\le u\le1-z.$$ For $\beta>0$, define $k_\beta(v)=(v-\beta)_+/v^2$ for $v>0$ and $k_\beta(0)=0$. For $\beta=0$, set $k_0(v)=1/v$ for $v>0$. Then $$\label{thinning:interval-bound}
 \int_u^{u+z}k_\beta(v)\,dv
 \le-\frac32\log(1-\gamma z).$$ If $x>0$, the endpoint $z=\gamma$ is also allowed. At $z=0$, both sides are zero.
Every state on [thinning:path] satisfies $$\label{thinning:window-bound} \int_q^s\frac{(h-b)_+}{h^2}\,dh\le3\kappa.$$

Let $x\ge0$, $d>0$, and $x+d<1$. Define $$\bar h(x,d)=\frac{H(x+d)+H(x-d)}2,\qquad
 e_0(x,d)=(1-x)H\!\left(\frac d{1-x}\right).$$ For every $e_0(x,d)\le e\le\bar h(x,d)$, $$\label{thinning:high-value-bound}
 \mathcal K(x,d,e)\ge
 J_0(x,d,e):=F(H(x)-e)-F(\bar h(x,d)-e).$$

For $|m|<1$ and $L/2\le I<H(m)$, $$\mathcal B_m(I)\ge F(I).
 \label{upgrade:high-information-bound}$$ The inequality is strict if $m\ne0$. Consequently a state with $F(I)>\mathcal B_m(I)$ must have $I<L/2$.

Let $m,d>0$, $m+d<1$, and $$0<e\le\bar h(m,d):=\frac{H(m+d)+H(m-d)}2.$$ Put $I=H(m)-e$, $j=\bar h(m,d)-e$, and $J=I-j$. If $I\le L/2$, then at fixed $d,e$, $$\partial_m\{F(I)-F(j)\}>0.
 \label{wall:positive-derivative}$$ At $j=0$, the derivative is interpreted from the physical side.

Let $(A,B)$ have a joint law on $[-1,1]^2$ with $e_a=\mathbb EH(A)>0$ and $e_b=\mathbb EH(B)>0$. Put $$a=\mathbb EA,\quad b=\mathbb EB,\quad
 m=\frac{a+b}{2},\quad e=\frac{e_a+e_b}{2},\quad
 I=H(m)-e,$$ and $I_a=H(a)-e_a$, $I_b=H(b)-e_b$. Then $$\mathbb Ec(A,B)\ge
 \widehat{\mathcal B}_m(I)
 -\frac{\widehat{\mathcal B}_a(I_a)
             +\widehat{\mathcal B}_b(I_b)}2.
 \label{upgrade:local-inequality}$$
